subject: On-prem deployment checkpoint: module review and rollback criteria
messages:
From: Alyssa Tran <alyssa.tran@acmecloud.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dan Wu <dan.wu@enterpriseco.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Private deployment module passoff — schedule request

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our infra team (cc'd) wants a dedicated review of the Terraform/Helm/Ansible artifacts you plan to ship for our on-prem rollout. Key asks from our side: network segmentation details, egress controls, KMS integration, and a clear rollback/playback plan for release failures.

Can we schedule 60 minutes tomorrow for a gates/acceptance pass? We'll want to include our security lead (Dan) and a systems engineer. I attached the internal checklist we'll use.

Best,
Alyssa
Alyssa Tran
Head of Cloud Architecture, Acme Cloud
---
Attachment: acme_priv_deploy_checklist.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Tran <alyssa.tran@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Dan Wu <dan.wu@enterpriseco.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment module passoff — schedule request

Alyssa — thanks for the checklist. We can do 60 minutes tomorrow at 10:30 PT. I'll run a pre-read for your team so the session focuses on gaps and acceptance criteria.

Pre-read items attached: a snapshot of the Terraform modules (redwood_onprem_modules.tf), the Helm values we intend to install behind the private registry (helm-chart-values.yaml), and the runbook for automated rollback (privdeploy-runbook.md).

High-level agenda for the call:
- Module layout & ownership (TF/Helm/Ansible boundaries)
- Network topology & firewall rules (subnet mapping, egress gateways)
- Secrets & KMS/HSM integration path
- CI gating & smoke tests (pre-apply plan + post-deploy probes)
- Rollback criteria and automated playbooks
- Audit logs and retention for compliance

If that works I’ll send a calendar invite and a short preflight script your SREs can run.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Private Deployments — Redwood Inference
---
Attachments: redwood_onprem_modules.tf (text/x-terraform), helm-chart-values.yaml (text/yaml), privdeploy-runbook.md (text/markdown)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Alyssa Tran <alyssa.tran@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 11:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment module passoff — schedule request

Adding a few notes ahead of the call so we can be concrete tomorrow: 

1) Terraform modules: the redwood_onprem_modules.tf bundle is split into three layers (network, infra, platform). For acceptance we need clear input/output contracts — specifically how the network module exposes NVA/egress gateway IPs to the infra module. Please confirm that the modules are idempotent and that state locking is enforced via our remote backend (S3 + DynamoDB) in customer-managed mode.

2) Helm/Operator: helm-chart-values.yaml contains a "privateRegistry" block — ensure imagePullSecrets are referenced through KMS-wrapped creds, not plaintext secrets in values.yaml. We'll prefer a sealed-secrets pattern if Acme's cluster supports it.

3) Ansible/Runbook: privdeploy-runbook.md should enumerate the manual-only steps vs automated playbooks. For rollback, we expect:
   - automatic KV cache flush,
   - scale-down of new replica set,
   - orchestrated KV restore from last snapshot if health checks fail for 3 rolling windows,
   - a documented human-approval path within 15 minutes.

4) CI gating: the pipeline we want is: plan-only -> terragrunt/terraform fmt & validate -> terraform plan (diff) -> security static checks (tfsec, kube-bench) -> plan review -> apply with canary rollout in Helm (10% traffic for 10 minutes) -> post-deploy smoke checks -> promote. Please bring the pipeline YAML or link tomorrow.

I noted a potential network gap: egress policy for third-party telemetry. We need explicit deny-by-default rules and allowlist for collector endpoints.

I’ll be on the call to walk through the TF state backend and the pipeline gate.

-Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Sr. Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Alyssa Tran <alyssa.tran@acmecloud.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dan Wu <dan.wu@enterpriseco.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 08:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment module passoff — schedule request

Thanks — that agenda works. A couple clarifications before the call: 

- For state backend, Acme requires state files never land on vendor-managed stores. We'll run S3 in our VPC (customer-owned) and expect Terraform to use the DynamoDB lock table we own. Can you confirm the modules support a backend override?

- For canary traffic routing: can you show how the 10% is enforced at the ingress layer? We use Envoy with traffic-splitting and need an annotation or service mesh config.

- On KMS: we have an HSM-backed KMS available in our HSM cluster. We'll want a short integration test (encrypt/decrypt cycle) as part of CI.

We’ll be on the 10:30 PT slot. See you then.

—Alyssa

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Tran <alyssa.tran@acmecloud.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Dan Wu <dan.wu@enterpriseco.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 09:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment module passoff — schedule request

Quick answers ahead of the meeting and pointers we'll demo:

- Backend override: all TF modules include a backend.tf.tmpl that supports backend configuration via environment variables or a backend override file. We'll demo applying the module with Acme's remote backend (customer S3 + DynamoDB lock) in dry-run mode.

- Canary routing: we implement canary via Helm chart annotations for the Envoy ingress (x-envoy-upstream-weight) plus a traffic-split CRD held in the mesh. We'll show the Helm values for the 10% split and the post-deploy Prometheus-based health gate that flips weights.

- KMS/HSM: the CI includes an integration test step that invokes the HSM-backed KMS endpoint (encrypt/decrypt) using a customer-scoped role. We will run this against a mocked HSM in CI and then against your HSM in the preflight stage.

- Rollback: the runbook contains a hitlist and an automated workflow (Ansible playbook) that will perform the scale-down + KV restore sequence. We also have a manual rollback play that opens a P0 channel and requires two-site approval.

We’ll attach the pipeline YAML during the session and mark the specific gates as 'blocking' vs 'informational'. Looking forward to aligning.

Regards,
Vivek
---
Calendar invite sent for 2026-12-16 10:30 PT (60m)
